components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one main action of a view.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; height: 48px; padding: 0 24px; border-radius: 9999px; background: #1463ff; color: #ffffff; font: 600 16px/1 Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; text-decoration: none; transition: background-color 150ms; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #1257df; } .ds-btn-primary:active { background: #0d4ac2; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #1463ff; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: A second action on a light surface.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; height: 48px; padding: 0 24px; border: 1px solid #535768; border-radius: 9999px; background: transparent; color: #0f0d16; font: 600 16px/1 Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; text-decoration: none; transition: background-color 150ms; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: #e7ecff; } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #1463ff; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: On-navy Button
components.description: A second action on a navy band.
components.html: See what it does
components.css: .ds-navy { padding: 24px; background: #061029; } .ds-btn-on-navy { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; height: 48px; padding: 0 24px; border: 1px solid rgb(255 255 255 / 0.2); border-radius: 9999px; background: transparent; color: #ffffff; font: 600 16px/1 Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; text-decoration: none; transition: background-color 150ms; } .ds-btn-on-navy:hover { background: rgb(255 255 255 / 0.1); } .ds-btn-on-navy:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #4d8bff; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Icon Button
components.description: The secondary style as a 48px circle around a 20px lucide icon, for controls such as the security cards' pause, previous and next. Pressed, it settles to 96%.
components.html: <button class="ds-btn-icon" type="button" aria-label="Next card"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m9 18 6-6-6-6"/></svg></button>
components.css: .ds-btn-icon { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 48px; height: 48px; padding: 0; border: 1px solid #535768; border-radius: 9999px; background: transparent; color: #0f0d16; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 150ms, scale 100ms; } .ds-btn-icon:hover { background: #e7ecff; } .ds-btn-icon:active { scale: 0.96; } .ds-btn-icon:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #1463ff; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-icon svg { width: 20px; height: 20px; fill: none; stroke: currentColor; stroke-width: 2; stroke-linecap: round; stroke-linejoin: round; }

components.name: Tinted Card

A phone inside the CRM

components.name: Callout
components.description: A statement that must stand out, such as how Google account data is used.
components.html:
How we use the data of your Google account

Every1Connects uses the access you give to your Gmail mailbox for two things only.

components.name: Badge
components.description: A short label; the status variant adds a success or warning dot.
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; padding: 2px 8px; border-radius: 6px; background: #e7ecff; color: #0f0d16; font: 500 12px/1.45 Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-dot { width: 8px; height: 8px; border-radius: 9999px; background: #4ec375; }

components.name: Carousel Segments
components.description: Under the security cards, one segment per card: a 4px line track that fills with primary while its card shows (5s), the ones before it full. Each is a button to its card.
components.css: .ds-segs { display: flex; gap: 8px; width: 320px; } .ds-seg { position: relative; flex: 1; height: 20px; padding: 0; border: 0; background: none; cursor: pointer; } .ds-seg::before, .ds-seg::after { content: ""; position: absolute; top: 8px; left: 0; height: 4px; border-radius: 9999px; } .ds-seg::before { right: 0; background: #d0d4e4; } .ds-seg::after { width: 0; background: #1463ff; } .ds-seg.is-done::after { width: 100%; } .ds-seg.is-on::after { width: 45%; }

narrative.overview:
A dealership showroom at opening time: a bright, uncluttered floor, even light, and the product placed where it can be seen whole. A cool gray canvas and white cards keep the floor calm, near-black Inter does the talking, and one saturated blue marks every action. Deep navy bands frame the hero and the closing call to sign in, and the CRM's real screens stand on the floor like the cars.

Calm and exact in type and color, soft in shape. From Close: one saturated blue as the only action color, Inter with tight tracking at large sizes, near-black ink and deep navy bands, few shadows, green and gold kept for status. From monday.com: the cool gray canvas with white cards, pill buttons and 24px cards, pale tinted surfaces, the wide soft card shadow, and an 8px rhythm with generous section spacing.

Left out on purpose: Close's square corners and blue-on-blue surfaces, monday's Poppins and light headlines, violet as an action color, the rainbow prism, gradient text and the bright tints. One theme; the navy bands are part of it, not a dark mode.
keyCharacteristics: One blue for every action; nothing else competes with it.
A surface change before a shadow.
The CRM's own screens as the only imagery.
The text of every page readable without JavaScript.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: Blue is the only action color. Another chromatic color never marks something clickable.

rules.name: The Readable Blue Rule
rules.body: Link text uses link (#1257df), which passes 4.5:1 on every light surface; primary (#1463ff) is for fills. On navy, blue text is primary-bright (#4d8bff).

rules.name: The Tight Top Rule
rules.body: Tracking tightens only from 20px up. Text of 18px and below has none, apart from the eyebrow.

rules.name: The Two Weights Rule
rules.body: Headings never go below 600 and text never goes above 400. Emphasis inside text is strong at 600 in ink.

rules.name: The Border-or-Shadow Rule
rules.body: A card has a border or a shadow, never both. The sticky header has neither.

dos: Do give a view one primary button; other actions are secondary buttons or links.
Do put ink and ink-soft text on tints, and link for links there.
Do make anything clickable at least 44px high.
Do reach for a surface change before a shadow.
Do keep every page's text in the server-rendered HTML; client-side script may add interaction, never hold the content.
Do keep the link to the privacy policy in the footer of every page.
Do keep the name reading Every1Connects everywhere; the logo's alt is site.name.
donts: Don't use primary as a text color on a tint or on navy.
Don't color text with a tint, success or warning.
Don't add a second typeface, or a weight other than 400, 500 and 600.
Don't add gradients beyond the glow of the hero and the closing band, and never on text.
Don't pick a radius, a gap or a font size that is not in DESIGN.md.
Don't put content behind script; text that appears only after JavaScript runs is invisible to a reviewer or crawler.

motion.name: state-change
motion.purpose: Color, background and border changes on hover and focus.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: A pressed pill button settles to 98%; an icon button to 96%.

motion.name: enter
motion.purpose: An element coming into view: the hero's notices (in the order of their times, 0.35s apart) and record, the product section's window and, below lg, each step's panel, the email section's cards and pictures (panel mask, window, then what is inside in order), the security cards (dealt in from the right 0.14s apart, each icon rising last) and the closing band's sign-in card (rising and growing from 95%, then its parts in reading order, 0.09s apart).

motion.name: exit
motion.purpose: An element leaving while still on screen: upward once a third of it is under the header (a tall one when its bottom edge reaches the top third), downward when its top edge reaches the bottom tenth. It comes back from the side it is on. The sign-in card's parts leave first, last to first, and the card after them.

motion.name: screen-change
motion.purpose: The product section's window changing to the screen of the step being read.

motion.name: autoplay
motion.purpose: The security cards play by themselves. They stop while the pointer is on them, while anything in them has keyboard focus, while they are off screen and when the pause button is pressed (WCAG 2.2.2).

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: With prefers-reduced-motion, things fade without moving and the security cards start paused. Without JavaScript nothing is hidden. Text never moves, except inside the security cards, which carry theirs.
